explanation: The first column must have eigenvalue −1. For v=(1,1,1), Av=(−1,−1,−1)=−v. The supplied second and third columns have eigenvalues 1 and 3, respectively, so AP=PD. These eigenvectors have distinct eigenvalues and are linearly independent, ensuring P is invertible. Thus option d works; any nonzero scalar multiple of v also works.
